deck: Table Rock this morning: 908.92 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Warm the hands, not the water.
play.body: Fish the warmest part of the afternoon on the lake. Fish first light on the trout water. Different climates.

season.name: Winter trout
season.why: Table Rock gets quiet and vertical. Taneycomo becomes the reason you came. This is Johnny Morris water — cold, clear, and honest.
tips: Spoon or ice jig over 30–50 feet on Table Rock if you must. Most people shouldn't.
Taneycomo is the trip: midges, eggs, pink worms, tiny jigs, 2-pound test.
Generation still rules. A winter blowdown is a drift day.
Felt soles and a staff if you wad. The rocks don't care that you're on vacation.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 909.37 early in the week to 908.92 this morning — about 0.45 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: The lake is down nearly 6 ft from full pool, exposing more shoreline, stumps and hazards in the coves, arms and near some ramps. Boat slowly in the James, Kings and Long Creek arms. Surface water is cold now, pushing bass tighter to structure.

Look for them on long points, gravel flats that drop into deeper water, and offshore brush piles in 20-40 ft. Jigs, drop-shot rigs, tubes and live bait are producing when presentations are slow and natural. Clarity is excellent, so light line and subtle moves win. Walleye continue to hold on points in 20-25 ft, with crappie working deeper brush and docks.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~300 cfs on the last printed reading. Not a live hourly. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: Cold bottom releases from Table Rock keep the tailwater in the low-to-mid 50s. Generation remains the tactic book: low morning flows open wading and light-line drifting with indicators. When units come online (often afternoons), switch to heavier setups and target seams, current breaks and structure from a boat or dock.

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek it is artificial lures and flies only — no soft plastics and no scented or natural baits. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released (slot limit). Save pink worms, PowerBait or other soft plastics/scented baits for water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required to keep fish. Always check the SWPA schedule or call 866-494-1993 before wading.

editor.note: Two-lake daily rebuilt from the morning fishing scout plus the prior week of files. We print a level only when the scout had one. Carry-forward mornings are labeled. No invented bite ratings. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
